newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Republic halts shipment of gene-spliced corn.
newsitem.headline: Czech Republic halts shipment of gene-spliced corn.

text.p: The Agriculture Ministry Friday halted a shipment of U.S. corn thought to contain genetically-engineered strains, pending further study on its effects.
Until the study is finished no corn from the shipment will be distributed in the Czech Republic, it added.

"The state Veterinary Administration is halting the shipment of maize (corn) ... until it is decided whether these genes can pass into the food chain," Frantisek Havir of the ministry's agriculture production section said.
He added that the Institute for Agricultural Production would conduct the study as soon as possible.
The Czech Republic does not have any laws regulating how genetically manipulated products should be treated.

It is illegal to market such modified corn in the European Union and a EU Commission is due to decide next week whether to allow imports of such modified corn, produced in the United States under license by Swiss chemical company Ciba Geigy.
U.S. exporters do not separate the engineer corn, estimated to amount to 0.6 percent of their crop, from conventional corn.
The exact location of the 33,000-ton shipment was unknown.
